title: Compact Session Protocol and Batched Tool Calls — PRD (WIP)
content:
Purpose

Short: define a lightweight session protocol and first-class support for batching tool calls from the Hosted API to reduce per-token overhead and improve developer ergonomics for stateful conversational flows.

Context and motivation

Problem statements we see in customer traces and SDK feedback:
- Long-running conversational sessions create a lot of small, repetitive RPCs for tool invocation (search, DB lookups, function call scaffolding). Each roundtrip adds latency and increases per-request cost.
- Mobile and edge clients need a compact on-wire representation for session resume and offline sync; current checkpoint snapshots are verbose.
- Developers want predictable behavior when a tool call fails mid-stream: automatic retries, retries coalescing, and clear failure semantics.
- SDK ergonomics around partial/structured output are fragmented: teams either parse free text or rely on heavyweight JSON schemas.

Objectives (what success looks like)
- Reduce average tool-call-related RPCs per session by 40% for benchmarked assistants that make frequent small lookups.
- Cut typical session resume payload size by 60% vs today’s full transcript snapshots.
- Offer an SDK surface that makes batched tool calls easy to implement and safe by default (idempotency, lease semantics, retry policies).
- Provide a progressive structured-output mode where partial frames can be validated incrementally and merged deterministically client-side.

Non-goals
- This PRD does not attempt to replace the existing streaming framing entirely. We will interoperate with current streaming protocols.
- Not addressing multi-party session federation (cross-account stitching) in v1.

Key concepts and terminology
- Session snapshot: a compact binary/JSON envelope that encodes minimal tokens, KV cache markers, and a small operation log for resumability.
- Delta frames: canonical minimal diffs produced by the model runtime describing additions to the transcript, tool call intents, and structured fragments.
- Tool batch: a single grouped request that contains multiple tool invocation intents (searches, function calls) originating from one or more delta frames and executed atomically by Redwood’s tool router.
- Tool lease: a short-lived idempotency token assigned to a batched tool call to support retries and cross-region fallback.

Proposed features (v1)
1) Compact session protocol
- Minimal envelope fields: session_id, version, sequence_cursor, kv_markers (list of short hashes), recent_delta_hashes (for de-dup), and an attachments pointer.
- Snapshot formats: JSON-lite for human visibility (development mode) and gzipped binary for production (sdk->hosted) to reduce bytes.
- Stitching rules: when resuming, the server will accept an overlapping cursor and replay only missing delta frames; conflict resolution is last-writer-wins per sequence_cursor.
- Server API endpoints: POST /sessions/:id/snapshot (upload), GET /sessions/:id/snapshot (download), POST /sessions/:id/repair (repair with client-supplied deltas).

2) Batched tool calls
- Client SDKs mark tool intents in outgoing request body as an array of intents with optional intent-scopes, priorities, and idempotency keys.
- Server groups intents by destination (same downstream connector) and executes as a single batched RPC where supported.
- Tool router returns a batched response with per-intent subresults; the runtime emits delta frames referencing the subresult ids.
- Atomicity modes: best-effort (default), per-batch-atomic (all-or-none), and isolated (no coalescing) selectable by client. Default is best-effort to maximize throughput.
- Tool lease issuance: each batch returns a lease token valid for 30s; SDKs should attach it when re-submitting a replayed batch after transient failure.

3) Structured incremental output (canonical delta frames)
- Every delta frame can carry a typed payload: {type: TEXT|STRUCT|TOOL_INTENT|META, schema_version: v1, payload: ...}.
- STRUCT payloads are small JSON fragments conforming to lightweight schemas (field names, basic types, optional constraints). Schemas can be inline or referenced by id.
- Clients can request partial validation: server will run schema checks on emitted STRUCT fragments and include validation hints in the telemetry block.

4) SDK ergonomics and high-level API surfaces
- New SDK primitive: Session.checkpoint({compact:true}) -> returns small snapshot blob and a human-readable debug summary.
- SDK helper: Tools.batch([intent, intent, ...], {atomicity: 'best-effort'}) -> returns a BatchHandle with awaitable results and built-in retries.
- Streaming adaptor: DeltaStream.on('delta', handler) where handler receives canonical delta frame objects (typed). The adaptor accepts an option to collapse repeated text deltas into a progressive text buffer.
- Client default behaviors: tool intents are automatically annotated with idempotency keys (UUIDs) unless the developer supplies one. SDKs expose a single opt-in switch for preserving raw token stream vs canonical deltas.

Telemetry and observability
- New metrics: tool_batch_size_histogram, batch_coalesce_rate, snapshot_bytes_saved, delta_replay_count, tool_lease_misuse_rate.
- Tracing: each batch gets a trace id; delta frames include trace breadcrumbs for cross-service correlation.
- Debug mode: snapshots include an annotated delta timeline to aid replaying client bugs.

Security and compliance considerations
- Snapshots may contain sensitive data. Production snapshots must be encrypted at rest with customer keys (apply existing KMS hooks).
- Tool batches involving connectors with differing access controls must be inspected; cross-connector batching restricted until connectors opt-in.
- Leases are bearer tokens; limit lifetime and scope and log issuance/consumption.

Performance tradeoffs and heuristics
- Batch coalescing heuristic: collect intents for up to 35ms or until 8 intents reached (configurable per route). Tunes latency vs throughput.
- Snapshot compaction: keep last N delta hashes (default N=16) in snapshot to speed dedup; beyond that, rely on server-side archival.
- Memory: server maintains transient batch buffers for 100ms for each active session; capacity planning required for high concurrency customers.

Compatibility and migration
- Backwards-compat: clients not adopting the new SDK will continue to receive classic streaming output. Server will emit both classic and canonical deltas when client negotiates dual-mode.
- Migration path: provide a lightweight shim in SDKs that converts older tool-call patterns into batched intents with minimal code changes (wrap existing calls with Tools.batch).
- Feature flags: phased rollout: internal dogfood -> opt-in beta tenants -> default enable for small sessions -> full rollout.

API sketches (examples)
- Batched tool call request (JSON-lite):
  {
    "session_id": "s-1032",
    "intents": [
      {"id":"i-1","target":"search","query":"find doc about billing","scope":"user:read","priority":"low"},
      {"id":"i-2","target":"vector-search","query":"embedding:…","priority":"high"}
    ],
    "atomicity":"best-effort"
  }

- Delta frame emitted after batch:
  {
    "seq": 421,
    "type": "TOOL_RESULT_BATCH",
    "batch_id": "b-81",
    "results": [ {"intent_id":"i-1","status":"ok","ref":"r-9"}, {"intent_id":"i-2","status":"ok","ref":"r-10"} ]
  }

SDK usage pattern (pseudo):
- await Tools.batch([intent1, intent2], {atomicity:'best-effort'})
- on delta: if delta.type == 'STRUCT' -> mergeStructured(delta.payload)
- when network flaps: save Session.checkpoint({compact:true}), resume later with POST /sessions/:id/repair

Rollout and success metrics
- Staged rollout over 8 weeks. Success criteria for GA: tool-batch_coalesce_rate > 0.35 for targeted customers, median added latency due to coalescing < 12ms, snapshot_bytes_saved median > 50%.

Open questions / risks
- Cross-connector privacy: what connectors should be allowed to co-batch? Need legal OK for cross-store aggregation.
- Lease semantics complexity: how to guarantee idempotency for connector operations that are not idempotent by nature?
- SDK surface proliferation: avoid many rarely used flags; prioritize one clear path for most developers.

Next steps / action items
- Engineering: prototype server-side batch router + simple connector adapter (2 sprints). Owner: Ravi.
- SDK: implement Session.checkpoint and Tools.batch in JS SDK, include debug mode. Owner: Lena.
- Product: prepare beta tenant list and dogfood scenarios. Owner: Maya.
- SRE: run capacity simulation for batch buffers and snapshot storage. Owner: Gabe.

Appendix: short sample timeline
- Week 1–2: spec finalize, prototype wire format, SDK API sketches.
- Week 3–5: internal dogfood, connectors adaptors for 2 high-volume connectors (search/kv).
- Week 6: private beta with 4 customers, measure metrics and iterate.
- Week 7–8: GA readiness checklist and roll out flags.

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally conservative in atomicity choices to avoid surprising developer semantics. Looking for feedback on: default coalescing thresholds, schema versioning approach for STRUCT deltas, and whether to provide a higher-level orchestration primitive that converts model-tool-tool sequences into a single named workflow.
